title: Record
description: One link in a role's continuity chain. This is the SPINE only: fixed-shape, prose-free, canonically encoded under canon/v1, hash-chained, and retained forever. The record's prose lives in a content-addressed blob referenced by body_digest and is erasable — deleting it leaves a tombstone and the chain still verifies. Every identifier a transition needs is here rather than in the body, because the fold must be computable from the chain alone.

v.description: Spine version. Distinct from scheme: a record's SHAPE and the BYTES a shape hashes to change for different reasons and must move separately.

scheme.description: The canonical encoding these bytes were produced under. Hashed INTO the digest, so a scheme mismatch presents as a mismatched digest rather than as a field a reader may ignore.

prev.description: Digest of the record at seq-1; empty at genesis. This is the compare-and-swap: to append you must present the tip you read, which is what makes two incarnations unable to both hold the role.

tenant.description: Root of every namespace and partition key of every chain, log, blob and anchor.

role.description: The durable office this chain belongs to. Colon-separated segments let human:mh, lead:platform and ic:contracts-org all be role ids under one rule — the human is a role like any other.

kind.description: The record kind. Open vocabulary on the wire: a reader that does not know a kind decides what to do from kind_class, not from this field.

kind_class.description: Carried on the wire rather than derived from a table, because the kinds a reader must classify correctly are exactly the ones missing from its own table. An unknown STRUCTURAL kind refuses the fold; an unknown ADVISORY kind is preserved verbatim and skipped. The failure this prevents: an old reader silently skipping a takeover concludes it still holds the role — two holders, produced by routine version skew, with every hash valid.

incarnation.description: The disposable session that wrote this record, identified by the digest of the attach or takeover that minted it. Absent on charter, attach and takeover — a record cannot contain its own digest. Digests rather than counters: a guessable id is one a re-reading writer copies by accident.

fence.description: The chain position this writer's authority was minted at. Long-lived verifiers keep a per-role high-water mark and refuse a lower fence. Fences are enforced by long-lived verifiers ONLY: an ephemeral CI runner's high-water mark is always zero and enforces nothing.

at.description: Stamped by the HOME, never by the agent. No refusal anywhere in this contract depends on this field: no refusal may depend on a clock the refusing party does not own.

body_digest.description: Reference to the erasable blob carrying this record's prose. Absent for most structural records.

body_class.description: Classification the blob store keys retention, encryption and erasure on. Required whenever body_digest is present: an unclassified blob has no retention rule, and the store cannot invent one at the moment someone asks for the erasure.

refs.description: What this record was derived from, each carrying its trust. The chain records CLAIMS by an incarnation; only broker outcomes are facts, and a prompt-injected checkpoint is durable and inherited by every future incarnation. Labelling the source is one of two structural mitigations that bound the blast radius; the other is that permitted effect classes are pinned in the charter.

next_due.description: The deadline the writer itself declares for its own next append. Liveness is derived against this, never from self-report — so an incarnation that hangs without exiting is correctly seen as dead.

subject.description: The transition's structural parameter. One fixed shape with optional members rather than a per-kind union, so there is exactly one canonical form for every kind; which members a kind requires is contract law in Go, not a schema constraint.

work.description: A work URI with a scheme: github:acme/api#88, jira:PROJ-412, dossier:proj/phase/task. The scheme is the single field deciding whether this substrate attaches to work an organization already has, or only ever works for one tracker.

digest.description: Pins the work item's content at assignment time, so a renamed or rewritten ticket reads as drift rather than being silently absorbed.

party.description: A role id: the supervisor on a takeover, the assignee on an assign, the child on a delegate, the target on a split or merge.

effect.description: An effect id, on intent-ref and on the resolution that closes one.

target.description: An earlier record this one acts on: the annulled record, the escalation a resolution closes.

terms.description: The inherited charter. Present only on charter and recharter; any other kind carrying it is refused charter_immutable. Immutability is not tidiness: if each incarnation could rewrite the goal, a role's purpose would be subject to a dozen rounds of lossy re-summarization with nothing to compare against.

scope.description: The work references this role owns. At least one: there is no unscoped role. A lead's scope is a scope, a maintainer's an area, an IC's a task — one rule covers all three because the URI scheme carries the difference.

tier.description: Inert, and no longer settable. Retained only because the canonical projection includes it, so dropping it would change every charter digest; nothing reads it. Risk is decided where the evidence is: a classifier floors a change, a grant ceilings the exact head. Retire at the next scheme bump.

effect_classes.description: What the role may do to the outside world. Bounds an injected incarnation to what the role could do anyway.

supervisors.description: The roles that may write a takeover against this one. The charter is the only place this can be stated: asking a holder to authorize its own replacement is exactly the case where it is unreachable.

cycle_ceiling.description: Encodes the two-fix-rounds review rule as an attenuating dimension instead of as prose an agent may or may not read. A looping panel becomes a refusal with a remedy rather than a silently burned budget.

min_reader.description: Monotone minimum reader version. A reader below it refuses the WHOLE chain rather than interpreting part of it — partial interpretation is how an old reader skips a takeover.

retire.description: The condition under which the role should be retired. An identifier-length phrase; the paragraph is body.
